title: night-bridge-shift-log-followups-2026-03-13
content:
Night bridge shift summary (overnight 2026-03-12 -> 2026-03-13)
Owner: Asha Patel (primary), Miguel Rivera (secondary)
Shift window: 22:00 - 06:00 PT

High-level summary:
- Two distinct incidents during the window: a short API error spike (22:45–23:10 PT) and an extended background KV eviction event (02:20–05:10 PT).
- Customer-visible impact: brief 502/500 spike for API routes to hosted inference (~3–5 min visible for some customers), longer degraded throughput for Dedicated routing while KV eviction sustained (affects tail latency).
- No P0 follow-up requested by Eng Leadership during shift, but SRE followups required for runbook gaps and monitoring tuning.

Timeline + actions taken:
- 22:43 PT: Pager: "API-500-Errors" fired (alert threshold p50 error rate > 2% across prod-api cluster). Notification to primary on-call.
  - Initial telemetry: error rate rose from 0.3% to 6.8% across prod-api. 5xx breakdown: 502 from routing-proxy (70%), 504 from serving-runtime (20%), 500 misc (10%).
  - Quick check: no rollout in progress (confirmed via release-engineering slack), connection pools at expected levels.
  - Mitigation: rolled back last non-hotfix traffic-shaping rule on routing-proxy (rolled back by Miguel, 22:50 PT). Error rate dropped to 1.1% by 22:55 PT, baseline restored by 23:05 PT.
  - Escalation: informed on-call infra lead (Chen Li) at 22:48 PT due to potential config drift.
  - Postmortem note: root cause likely an unintended traffic policy change that increased request fanout to a subset of serving-runtime instances; change came from console UI by an engineer in product-ops (linked in ticket INC-3241).

- 02:18 PT: Alert: "kv-cache-evictions-high" (redis eviction rate > 2000/s for 5m) and related queue backpressure metrics on serving-runtime GPU queues.
  - Observed: large number of cache TTL expiries after a job that prefetched embeddings for an internal batch job. Prefetch job spikes coincided with cache churn.
  - Impact: higher cold-starts for models on Dedicated pools; tail p95 latency increased from 180ms to 420ms for ~2k requests/min for ~3 hours.
  - Actions: throttled the internal prefetch job via cron override (Samira applied temporary job-limit at 02:35 PT), added temporary cache-connection backoff to one misbehaving worker (Chen patched and restarted the worker container at 02:50 PT).
  - Mitigation status: traffic and eviction rate reduced by 03:10 PT, but latent queue depth continued to cause increased p95 until we manually increased worker concurrency on a subset of pools at 04:20 PT (Miguel). Full recovery to baseline by 05:10 PT.
  - Customer comms: SCS notified two Dedicated customers impacted via internal ticket SRE-789. No public incident page created; product impact was limited and tracked with account owners.

Known gaps identified during shift:
- Runbook: cache-eviction runbook exists but does not include instructions for prefetched-batch-job identification (missing query snippets to map job IDs to caches). Proposed change: add "detect-prefetch-job" query and escalation path to data-team. Owner: Samira Khan. Deadline: 2026-03-20.
- Alerts: API error alert threshold and routing-policy-change detection are separate; we should add an alert that correlates sudden routing-proxy policy updates with error spikes (low-noise). Owner: Chen Li. Ticket: SRE-790.
- Playbook: no clear temporary throttle mechanism documented for internal cron jobs that interact with cache. Add a short section to "internal-batch-ops" runbook with sample kubectl/cron override commands. Owner: Asha Patel. Deadline: 2026-03-18.

Action items (concrete)
- INC-3241: Follow up with product-ops on console permission audit to prevent accidental routing-policy edits. Owner: Miguel Rivera. Due: 2026-03-16.
- SRE-790: Implement correlated alert for routing-policy-change + error spike. Owner: Chen Li. Due: 2026-03-19.
- RB-234 (runbook update): Add prefetch-job detection queries and remediation steps to kv-cache runbook. Owner: Samira Khan. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Deploy a short-term dashboard tile for eviction rate vs. internal batch job slots to make correlation visible to on-call. Owner: Asha Patel. Due: 2026-03-17.

Follow-ups started during shift (not yet complete)
- Created Jira ticket INC-3241 with links to console audit logs, policy diff, and the rollback performed. Assigned to product-ops with SRE in watchers.
- Opened SRE-790 for alert correlation work; initial alert rule skeleton pushed to observability repo (branch: sre/alert-correlation). Need PR and rollout in monitoring.
- Drafted runbook diff and pushed as a Google Doc to product-runbooks for review (link in linked_artifacts).

Monitoring notes & metrics observed
- API 5xx spike: peak 6.8% at 22:46 PT, affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream primarily. Error logs show increased connection resets between routing-proxy and serving-runtime during the spike.
- KV evictions: sustained 2.4k/s evictions at 02:25 PT with Redis memory pressure at 78%. After throttling prefetch job, evictions dropped to 320/s by 03:20 PT and baseline ~40/s by 05:10 PT.
- GPU queue depth: p99 queue length rose from 1 to 6 in affected pools; worker concurrency bump dropped p99 back to 1.

Customer and GTM notes
- Two Dedicated accounts saw visible throughput degradation; account CS leads notified (ticket SRE-789). No escalations from customers overnight. Product team tracking to evaluate SLA credit eligibility if required.

Runbook/automation suggestions (quick ideas collected during shift)
- Automate temporary throttle: add a small API endpoint in internal admin plane to toggle batch-job concurrency for prefetch jobs without needing kube overrides. Low-effort, high-impact.
- Add a tag-based circuit breaker for routing-policy changes: any console change to routing policies should automatically create a draft change and require a second approver for changes that touch >10% traffic.

Notes to next shift (morning handoff)
- Check progress on INC-3241 and SRE-790 PRs. Expect follow-up review comments from product-ops.
- Watch eviction metrics for 24hrs to ensure no recurrence when daily prefetch window runs (morning batch at 09:00). If eviction rate > 800/s for more than 15m, escalate to oncall infra lead.
- Confirm the temporary cron throttle has been reverted if long-term fix is deployed; otherwise leave it in place until RB-234 is complete.

Loose questions / items to surface in post-incident review
- Why did the routing-policy change slip through console without an approver? UI/permissions gap or human error?
- Can we surface config diffs in the alert body automatically when routing-proxy policy changes?
- Should we introduce a staging traffic policy validation that simulates impact on a small percentage before applying to prod?

Attachments and links:
- INC-3241 (Jira): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3241
- SRE-789 (internal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-789
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Nightly-Bridge-Notes

Prepared by: Asha Patel
Primary contact for followups: asha@redwood.ai

Quick sign-off checklist for docs team: add short "what I changed" header to the runbook diffs (helps reviewers), mark items as draft/in-review, assign small PRs (<=1 day) for alert rule changes so we can iterate quickly.

End of shift log.
